models.summary: Six island states are chosen as the most exposed: Kiribati, Nauru, the Bahamas, the Marshall Islands, Tuvalu and the Maldives. A table gives each one's population, share of land below five meters, terrain height and annual sea-level rise, all close to 4 mm a year. Regression on past sea level plus the landform and population data gives a first estimate of 200,000 to 300,000 displaced people by 2080, restated later as 300,000 to 400,000. Anyone living below five meters counts as displaced.
models.purpose: Estimate how many people sea-level rise displaces by 2080.
objectives: Forecast the displaced population of six island states.

models.section: 3.2 Possible cultural loss due to transfer
models.summary: Six factors measure cultural-loss risk: nationalist tendency, the refugees' location, fit of production and lifestyle, the carrier a culture needs, refugee cohesion, and the culture's economic return. Principal components keep the roots with high contribution and use them as weights, giving Z as the weighted combination. Three monotone relations are stated: deeper cultural dependence lowers risk, stronger exclusion of outsiders raises it, and a more complicated carrier raises it.

models.summary: Fit between an origin and a destination has three parts: the destination's acceptance, the product of its education level and GDP per head; the refugees' adaptation, the share of earlier migrants who live stably; and natural factors, consumer-based carbon emissions divided by distance, so high emitters carry more duty. Weights 0.57, 0.34 and 0.08 come from a reciprocal comparison matrix. A worked case gives 2.0416. The scores weight a complete bipartite graph and the Kuhn-Munkres algorithm returns the best destination. Whole populations move together, and a destination may refuse once full.

models.summary: Five indicators stand for human-rights protection: education, medical care, grain, pensions and housing per person. Principal components give fixed weights 0.269, 0.054, 0.257, 0.279 and 0.309. Arrival dilutes each indicator because the same total is split over more people. With no policy the index falls as arrivals grow. Policy adds grain and adds a term in employment and tax revenue, so the index recovers. Births and deaths then enter the denominator, and the late stage is claimed to pass the pre-arrival level.
models.purpose: Track how protection per person falls on arrival and recovers under policy.
objectives: Show the path of the protection index with and without policy.

models.summary: Culture is split into three kinds by the sign of its economic effect. Art and intangible heritage always pay, and the gain compounds at the cultural sector's growth rate, scaled by how far policy pushes it into the market. Religion and custom always cost, through riots whose chance depends on tolerance and whose scale shrinks with ethnic diversity. Food, clothing and daily life switch at a tolerance of one half: above it they pay, below it they cost. A place with many groups finds a new balance without policy; a place with one group shows net loss.
models.purpose: Separate cultural effects into gain, loss and a switch, and time the balance point.
objectives: Quantify gain and loss by culture type and locate the balance.
